name: Motion Editor
description: Build a local, offline motion-design editor app (After Effects / Screen Studio-lite) with scenes, layers, keyframes, springs, presets, stagger, a cursor layer, timeline, undo/redo, save/open, and deterministic MP4 export.
prompt:
# Motion Editor

Use this skill when the user wants to build a local, offline motion-design editor app (After Effects / Screen Studio-lite). The deliverable is the editor itself, not a video.

Do not use this skill when:
- the user wants a single finished film (use `motion-film`)
- the request is a Manim explainer (use `manim-video`) or editing existing footage

Inputs:
- Output dir: {{output_dir}}
- Phase: {{phase}}

Workflow:
1. Resolve the app folder. If `{{output_dir}}` is empty, use `motion-editor` in the current workspace. Confirm the user's OS to adapt shortcuts (Cmd on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere).
2. Read `{baseDir}/SKILL.md` in full: it is the binding spec (environment, architecture, data model, phases, export, out-of-scope, verification, deliverable). Read `{baseDir}/references/techniques.md` for closed-form springs and the render/QA pipeline.
3. Keep `PROGRESS.md` in the app folder, recording what is built and which verifications passed. Resume from it when it already exists.
4. Stack: Vite + React + TypeScript, Zustand, zod, small Express server; Node 20+, ffmpeg in PATH. No AI/API calls at runtime. Justify any deviation in README.
5. Architecture: `project.json` is the single source of truth; one pure `renderFrame(project, timeSec, ctx, scale)` on Canvas 2D drives both preview and export. No `Date.now()`, unseeded randomness, CSS animations, or rAF-accumulated state.
6. Do not invent a video concept, demo content, or auto-render. First launch opens an empty project; rendering happens only on Export.
7. Build Phase 1 completely and verify it before Phase 2. If `{{phase}}` names a phase, focus there but respect that order.
8. Actually run the verification: unit tests (interpolation, every easing, determinism), the Playwright e2e flow, and the export frame-diff test. Do not claim untested features.
9. Write `{artifactDir}/progress-report.md` with built features, test results, and the run/render commands.
10. End with the app path, `npm install && npm run dev`, the CLI render command, and the README's "Works (tested)" / "Not implemented" / "Known limitations" summary.

Success criteria:
- The editor runs offline and passes the verification tests.
- README lists as working only what passed.

parameters.name: output_dir
parameters.description: Workspace-relative or absolute folder for the editor app

parameters.name: phase
parameters.description: Which part of the spec to focus on

routing.useWhen: Use when the user asks to build a motion editor, animation editor, keyframe timeline app, or a reusable tool for making motion-design videos.
routing.dontUseWhen: Do not use when the user wants a single finished film or promo video (use motion-film), a Manim explainer (use manim-video), or edits to existing video footage.
routing.outputs: A working offline Vite + React + Express motion editor with tests, PROGRESS.md, a README with tested/not-implemented/limitations sections, and a progress report under {artifactDir}.
routing.successCriteria: Phase 1 is verified before Phase 2; unit, e2e, and export tests actually run and pass; the README lists as working only what passed.
